Lower
lō'-ēr
adj. (comparative of low: beneath in place, in rank, or in glory)
Comparative of low. In the Authorized Version lower is a word of two very different histories: the humiliation into which Christ descended by choice, and the humiliation into which a proud man is put by another.

Biblical Definition

“Thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour” (Psa 8:5). The psalm says it of man as man — a creature ranked beneath the angels and yet crowned with dominion — and Hebrews takes it up and says it of the Son, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death. That is the deepest use of the word in Scripture: a voluntary lowering, a descent undertaken so that the crown might be given to the very nature that was lowered. The other uses stand around it. Noah's ark had “lower, second, and third stories” (Gen 6:16), a house of salvation built in ranks. The priest examining a plague looked to see whether it lay “lower than the skin” — depth being the mark of a leprosy that had gone in rather than remained upon the surface. Wisdom counsels the guest to take the low seat, “for better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince” (Pro 25:7) — the proverb our Lord repeats in Luke 14. And of the enemies of the righteous: “those that seek my soul, to destroy it, shall go into the lower parts of the earth” (Psa 63:9). The whole doctrine of humility is in the difference between going lower and being put lower.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines low as not high or elevated, depressed below the usual level, and humble in condition or rank; lower as its comparative.

expand to see more

LOW, a. Not high or elevated; depressed below any given surface or place.

1. Not elevated in rank or condition; humble; as men of low condition.

2. Humble in mind; not proud or aspiring; as a low and contrite spirit.

LOWER, v.t. To let down; to cause to descend; to bring low; to humble.

Key Scripture

Psa 8:5 — "For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour."

Pro 25:7 — "For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen."

Gen 6:16 — "A window shalt thou make to the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it."

Psa 63:9 — "But those that seek my soul, to destroy it, shall go into the lower parts of the earth."

Modern Corruption

Lowliness is treated as poor self-regard; Scripture treats it as accurate self-knowledge before God.

expand to see more

Modern usage has flattened lowly into a bruised self-image, and the counsel given is therefore to think better of oneself. Scripture never counsels a man to think better or worse of himself as such; it counsels him to think truly, and the truth is that he is a creature made a little lower than the angels, dust by origin and crowned by grace. The lowness commended in Proverbs 25:7 is not a low opinion but a low seat, chosen deliberately by a man who knows he has no claim to the high one. That is why the proverb ends in being called up: God exalts the man who took the honest place.

The second corruption is Christological and older. Because Hebrews applies Psalm 8 to the Son — made a little lower than the angels — some have reasoned from it to a Christ who is lesser in nature than the Father, or an angel Himself. The confessional answer is the state-of-humiliation doctrine: the Son, equal with the Father in essence, took to Himself a true human nature and in it submitted to the law, to suffering and to death, without any subtraction from His deity. He was lowered in state, never in nature.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew shaphal (H8213), to be low, to be brought low; tachti (H8482), lower, nether; Greek elattoo (G1642), to make less or lower.

expand to see more

Hebrew shaphal (H8213) — to sink, to be humbled, to be brought low; the standing verb behind Isaiah's bringing down of the lofty.

Hebrew tachti (H8482) — lower, nether, lowest; Genesis 6:16 (the lower story), Psalm 63:9 (the lower parts of the earth).

Hebrew me'at (H4592) — a little, a small amount; Psalm 8:5, made a little lower — a measure of degree, and in Hebrews of time.

Greek elattoo (G1642) — to make less, to lower; Hebrews 2:7, 2:9, John 3:30 (I must decrease).

Greek tapeinoo (G5013) — to make low, to humble; Philippians 2:8, He humbled himself.

Usage

"“A little lower than the angels” — said of man, and then of the Son."

"“Lower, second, and third stories” — even the ark of salvation had ranks."

"“Put lower in the presence of the prince” — the shame of taking the seat one had not earned."
